caption: The drawing features a detailed depiction of a knife with a distinctive handle and its accompanying sheath, shown from multiple angles on a tan background. The primary object is a large fixed-blade knife positioned vertically, with a handle shaped like a light-colored animal bone, complete with anatomical features and two visible rivets or screws. The guard is a thin, flat, copper or brass-colored piece separating the handle from the blade. The blade itself is broad, slightly curved, and depicted in shades of gray and brown with darker streaks and markings, suggesting aged or patterned metal. To the immediate right of the knife is a full-length side profile of its sheath; the sheath is brown and contoured to the knife’s shape, with light stitching along the edge and two buttoned straps for securing the knife. Two rectangular insets to the far right provide additional views: the upper inset shows the knife sheathed, with the bone handle and metal guard visible above the brown leather sheath, and distinct stitching along the front; the lower inset displays the sheathed knife frontally, now with decorative attachments on each side of the sheath, giving it the appearance of having "wings" or appendages. The background is a consistent, untextured tan, and the artist’s name, "JESS W. SMISEN," appears in the bottom right corner.
title: Sheath Knife
